app.name: Unmyst
app.description: Finally see through all your subscriptions and memberships in one place. Unmyst is a subscription manager that helps you track, manage, and cancel your subscriptions with ease.

footer.madeBy: Made by Aovee, because a spreadsheet stopped being funny.

hero.body: Unmyst is a subscription tracker. You enter each plan, its price, and its billing cycle; it converts everything to a comparable monthly figure and shows you when each one renews. It doesn't connect to your bank — you type in the numbers, and it does the arithmetic.

howItCounts.title: The same amounts, read three ways
howItCounts.intro: A weekly, monthly, and yearly plan can't be compared as they're billed. Unmyst shows your subscriptions three ways, each answering a different question. Nothing is invented — they're the same figures, grouped differently.

one.title: Levelled to a month
one.body: Every plan is reduced to what it costs per month, so plans on different cycles line up on one scale. A yearly price is divided by twelve; a weekly price is multiplied by 52 and divided by twelve. The real charge and its cycle stay visible on the same row.

two.title: Actually billed
two.body: What your bank is charged on the day it happens, each plan counted on its own cycle. Nothing is smoothed or averaged, so this is the figure that matches your statement — including the months a yearly plan lands.
two.formula: the real charge, on its real date

three.title: Averaged out
three.body: A budgeting estimate that spreads every plan evenly across weeks, months, and years. Nothing is ever billed this way; it exists to give you a single steady number to set aside, whichever month you look at.
three.formula: all plans, spread evenly over time

ledger.title: One list, ordered by what renews next
ledger.body: Your subscriptions page groups renewals into this week, later this month, and further out. Each row carries the real charge, the billing cycle, and the levelled monthly figure side by side, so nothing looks comparable by accident. The example shows three plans on two different cycles.

track.title: A handful of fields per plan
track.intro: Each subscription holds the details that change what it costs you. Only the service, price, cycle, and first billing date are required; the rest refine the figures.

cycles.title: Any billing cycle
cycles.body: Weekly, monthly, or yearly — plus an "every N cycles" option for the awkward ones, like a plan billed once every three months.

splits.title: Shared plans
splits.body: Split a cost equally between however many people share it, including you. Your share becomes the headline figure, with the full charge shown underneath.

trials.title: Free trials
trials.body: Mark a plan as starting on a trial. It counts as €0 today but still appears in your run-rate, and you can flag whether it converts to paid on its own.

categories.title: Categories
categories.body: Tag each plan — Entertainment, Music, Software, and so on — so the dashboard can break your spending down by category.

panels.title: Eight panels, all from the plans you enter
panels.intro: There's no separate setup. Add subscriptions and each panel fills in from them:

billed.title: Actually billed
billed.body: Real charges, grouped by weekly, monthly, and yearly.

trends.title: Spending trends
trends.body: What you'll be billed each month, month by month.

top.title: Top subscriptions
top.body: Your priciest plans, each levelled to a month.

category.title: By category
category.body: Monthly spend split across the categories you set.

creep.title: Subscription creep
creep.body: How your monthly run-rate has grown as plans were added.

averaged.title: Averaged out
averaged.body: The evened-out estimate, per week, month, and year.

renewals.title: Upcoming renewals
renewals.body: What's due next, including trials about to convert.

calendar.title: Renewal calendar
calendar.body: Every renewal this month laid out on a calendar.

data.title: Stored in your account, not pulled from your bank
data.body: You sign in with a one-time link sent to your email, or with Google — there's no password to set. Your subscriptions are saved to your account, so they're there on any device you sign in from. Unmyst has no connection to your bank or card and can't read transactions; every figure is one you entered yourself.

rows.storedValue: Price, cycle, dates, split, trial, category

limits.bank: Connect to your bank or read transactions — you enter what you pay.
limits.cancel: Cancel anything for you. It shows what's due; you cancel it yourself.
limits.guess: Guess at prices. A plan keeps the last figure you gave it until you change it.
limits.oneOff: Track one-off purchases. If it doesn't recur, it doesn't belong here.

cta.title: Start with the plans you already know
cta.body: Add a few subscriptions and the monthly total, the renewal dates, and the category breakdown fill in as you go. Entering a year's worth takes about ten minutes.
